title: Minimum Absolute Difference Between Elements With Constraint
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer x, find the smallest difference between any two elements where the indices of these elements are at least x apart.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer x, find the smallest difference between any two elements where the indices of these elements are at least x apart. Return the minimum absolute difference.
constraints: Choose two indices whose distance is at least x.
Return the minimum absolute difference between their values.
target_time_complexity: O(n²) with a list; O(n log n) with a balanced ordered set
hints: When processing index i, only values at indices through i-x are eligible.
Maintain those values in sorted order and inspect the insertion neighbors of nums[i].
Insert nums[i-x], binary-search nums[i], and update from successor and predecessor.
In a sorted set the closest value must be adjacent to the insertion point, so two checks suffice.
editorial: In a sorted set the closest value must be adjacent to the insertion point, so two checks suffice.

tests.explanation: Indices zero and three both contain four and are at least two apart, so the answer is zero.
The closest values at distinct eligible indices differ by one.
